newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico outlines Sept. reserves, assets.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico outlines Sept. reserves, assets.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Thursday that its net international assets as of September 30 were $3.423 billion, down from $3.864 billion on September 27.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of September 30 were $15.563 billion, down from $15.571 billion as of September 27.
It said the decrease in international assets reflected a combination of three factors:
- revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $145 million;
- net sales of $576 million to the federal government to cover debt-servicing charges;
- a foreign exchange decline of $10 million reflecting to various factors.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose by 287 million pesos in the September 27-30 period, while federal government deposits fell by 1.477 billion pesos.
Central bank credits for Fobaproa rose by 1.543 billion pesos, but the transaction had no monetary impact, it said.
Central bank credit to banks rose 2.821 billion pesos to meet the rising demand for notes and coins.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the International Monetary Fund and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
